facts.statement: Cerrejonisuchus is known from fossils found in the Cerrejón Formation in northeastern Colombia dating to the Paleocene.
facts.quote: It is known from a complete skull and mandible from the Cerrejón Formation in northeastern Colombia, which is Paleocene in age.

facts.statement: Specimens of Cerrejonisuchus were discovered in the Cerrejón open-pit coal mine in La Guajira, Colombia.
facts.quote: Specimens belonging to Cerrejonisuchus and to several other dyrosaurids have been found from the Cerrejón open-pit coal mine in La Guajira.

facts.statement: The snout of Cerrejonisuchus is the shortest of all dyrosaurids, measuring only 54-59% of the total skull length.
facts.quote: The length of the rostrum is only 54-59% of the total length of the skull, making the snout of Cerrejonisuchus the shortest of all dyrosaurids.

facts.statement: Cerrejonisuchus was the smallest known dyrosaur in terms of estimated body length.
facts.quote: Cerrejonisuchus was small for a dyrosaur, with the shortest estimated body length of any known dyrosaur.

facts.statement: The snout of Cerrejonisuchus is narrow and maintains a consistent width from the nostrils to the eye sockets.
facts.quote: The snout of Cerrejonisuchus is narrow and consistent in width from the external nares, or nostril openings, to the orbits, or eye sockets.

facts.statement: The nostrils of Cerrejonisuchus are located at the very tip of its snout.
facts.quote: The external nares are positioned extremely anteriorly at the very tip of the snout.

facts.statement: Cerrejonisuchus had generally uniform teeth, though the third upper jaw tooth was enlarged and the fourth was smaller.
facts.quote: The dentition of Cerrejonisuchus is generally homodont, although the third maxillary tooth is enlarged and the fourth is somewhat smaller than the rest.

facts.statement: Unlike many other dyrosaurids, the teeth of Cerrejonisuchus were not curved.
facts.quote: Unlike many other dyrosaurids, including Dyrosaurus maghribensis, Atlantosuchus coupatezi, Guarinisuchus munizi, Phosphatosaurus gavialoides, and Sokotosuchus ianwilsoni, the teeth of Cerrejonisuchus are not curved.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the short snout of Cerrejonisuchus was an adaptation for a generalized diet.
facts.quote: The short snout of Cerrejonisuchus is thought to be an adaptation to such a generalized diet.

facts.statement: Cerrejonisuchus lived during the Middle to Late Paleocene epoch.
facts.quote: Cerrejonisuchus is known from the Middle to Late Paleocene Cerrejón Formation.

facts.statement: Fossils of Cerrejonisuchus were found in sediments likely deposited in a brackish water river-to-lagoonal environment.
facts.quote: The section of the Cerrejón Formation from which fossils of Cerrejonisuchus have been found was likely deposited in a transitional environment, probably brackish water in a river-to-lagoonal setting.

facts.statement: A 2010 phylogenetic analysis placed Cerrejonisuchus basally in the dyrosaur clade between Phosphatosaurus and Arambourgisuchus.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis of dyrosaurids by Hastings et al. (2010) placed Cerrejonisuchus relatively basally in the dyrosaur clade between Phosphatosaurus gavialoides and Arambourgisuchus khouribgaensis.

facts.statement: Despite both having short snouts, Cerrejonisuchus is not closely related to Chenanisuchus, showing that snout shape does not determine phylogeny in dyrosaurs.
facts.quote: Although it might be expected that Chenanisuchus and Cerrejonisuchus are closely related because they are the only dyrosaurids with short snouts, the results of the analysis show that snout proportions alone are not indicative of phylogenetic relatedness in dyrosaurs.

facts.statement: The only known specimens of Cerrejonisuchus include a skull (type specimen), a lower jaw, a skull with partial skeleton, and a snout.
facts.quote: Currently the only known specimens of Cerrejonisuchus are UF/IGM 29 (skull, the type specimen), UF/IGM 30 (Lower jaw), UF/IGM 31 (Skull and partial postcranial skeleton), and UF/IGM 32 (Snout).

facts.statement: Closed neurocentral sutures in one specimen indicate that the individual had reached morphological maturity.
facts.quote: In UF/IGM 31, the neurocentral sutures of the anterior dorsal vertebrae are closed, an indication of morphological maturity.

facts.statement: Well-developed osteoderms likely indicate maturity, as they begin calcifying after one year in living crocodilians.
facts.quote: The presence of well-developed osteoderms is likely to be an indication that the animal was mature because in living crocodylians, the osteoderms begin calcification after 1 year and grow to articulate with other osteoderms to form a dermal shield at maturity.

facts.statement: An unfused nasal suture in one specimen suggests it was less mature than the others.
facts.quote: UF/IGM 32 has an unfused nasal suture, suggesting that it was less mature than the other individuals.

facts.statement: The age of the Cerrejón Formation is dated to the Middle-Late Paleocene using carbon isotopes, pollen, spores, and dinoflagellate cysts.
facts.quote: The age of the Cerrejón Formation has been dated as Middle-Late Paleocene based on carbon isotopes, pollen, spores, and dinoflagellate cysts.

facts.statement: Cerrejonisuchus may have served as a secondary food source for the giant snake Titanoboa in their shared brackish water habitat.
facts.quote: Cerrejonisuchus may have been a secondary food source for the primarily piscivorous Titanoboa, which would have lived in the same brackish water environment.

facts.statement: Its compressed, homodont teeth suggest a terrestrial predatory lifestyle, though its flat skull differs from other terrestrial crocodylomorphs.
facts.quote: The presence of homodont dentition with compressed teeth similar to those of sebecians and other terrestrial crocodylomorphs has been used as an argument for a terrestrial predatory lifestyle, though unlike other terrestrial crocodylomorphs it has a flat skull.

facts.statement: Compared to total skull length, the snout of Cerrejonisuchus is the shortest of any dyrosaurid.
facts.quote: Comparado a la longitud craneal total, el rostro de Cerrejonisuchus es el más corto de cualquier dirosáurido.

facts.statement: Along with Chenanisuchus and Anthracosuchus, Cerrejonisuchus is one of the only dyrosaurids with a short snout.
facts.quote: Junto a Chenanisuchus y Anthracosuchus, son los únicos dirosáuridos de hocico corto.

facts.statement: The nostrils of Cerrejonisuchus were positioned very far forward, almost at the tip of the snout.
facts.quote: Las fosas nasales están colocadas en una disposición muy anterior, casi en la punta del hocico.

facts.statement: The dentition of Cerrejonisuchus was generally homodont, although the third upper molar was elongated and the fourth was slightly smaller than the rest.
facts.quote: La dentición de Cerrejonisuchus es generalmente homodonta, aunque el tercer diente maxilar es alargado y el cuarto es algo menor que el resto.

facts.statement: Cerrejonisuchus likely had a diet consisting of fish, invertebrates, frogs, lizards, small snakes, and possibly mammals.
facts.quote: Cerrejonisuchus probablemente tenía una dieta consistente en peces, invertebrados, ranas, lagartos, pequeñas serpientes, y posiblemente mamíferos.

facts.statement: The short snout of Cerrejonisuchus is believed to be an adaptation for a generalist diet.
facts.quote: El corto hocico de Cerrejonisuchus se cree que es una adaptación para una dieta generalista.

facts.statement: With its shorter snout, Cerrejonisuchus may have been able to occupy a new ecological niche in the tropical rainforest environment of Paleocene Colombia.
facts.quote: Con su hocico más corto, Cerrejonisuchus pudo haber sido capaz de ocupar un nuevo nicho ecológico en el ambiente de selvas tropicales de la Colombia del Paleoceno.

facts.statement: Cerrejonisuchus is known from the middle to late Paleocene in the Cerrejón Formation.
facts.quote: Cerrejonisuchus es conocido desde mediados a finales del período Paleoceno en la formación Cerrejón.

facts.statement: The section of the Cerrejón Formation yielding Cerrejonisuchus fossils was likely deposited in a transitional environment, probably brackish water in a river and lagoon setting.
facts.quote: La sección de la formación Cerrejón de la cual se extrajeron los fósiles de Cerrejonisuchus fue probablemente depositada en un ambiente de transición, probablemente agua salobre en un entorno de río y lagunas.

facts.statement: The only known specimens of Cerrejonisuchus are UF/IGM 29 (holotype skull), UF/IGM 30 (lower jaws), UF/IGM 31 (skull and partial skeleton), and UF/IGM 32 (partial snout).
facts.quote: Actualmente los únicos ejemplares conocidos de Cerrejonisuchus son UF/IGM 29 (el cráneo holotipo), UF/IGM 30 (mandíbulas inferiores), UF/IGM 31 (cráneo y esqueleto parcial), y UF/IGM 32 (rostro parcial).

facts.statement: All specimens of Cerrejonisuchus come from the Cerrejón open-pit mine at Mina La Puente below Vein 90.
facts.quote: Todos los especímenes proceden de la mina a cielo abierto del Cerrejón en la mina La Puente debajo de la Veta de Carbón 90.
